goalAndTeaching.excerpt: A purpose is something a participant hopes to achieve. An understanding concerns what that participant believes an agreement establishes. Two participants can both decide to enter an agreement without explaining all of its terms in the same way.
goalAndTeaching.goal: Use a specific detail from a source to explain a treaty purpose or understanding, and distinguish the source's words from your own conclusion.
goalAndTeaching.whereTaught: Goal strip + section 1 'A purpose is not the same as an understanding' (3 paragraphs + organizer); reinforced in sections 2-6 and the take-forward.

workedResponse.finishedResponse: The textbook summary contrasts a government understanding of surrendering a claim to land with an understanding among First Nations leaders of sharing land (Source A, p. 26). Ahnassay's account adds a specific concern: Chief Chateh wanted his people's traditional lands protected into the future (Source B, p. 27). That detail helps explain why the difference between sharing and surrender matters in the source discussion. It is a retrospective account about a particular experience, so it does not establish what every treaty participant understood.
workedResponse.reasoningDemonstrated: claim → detail selection → connection explanation → scope limitation (6-part writing model compressed to the taught 4 steps; limitation explicit).
